timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Parliament, Regions.
All right, we're very rapidly running out of time.
A couple of quick issues. Greg Hunt, in terms of debate,
there's also, against the question of follow through.
And what do we make of the quality of discussion?
When immediately after the last federal budget,
the coalition was very loud about its opposition to the government's cuts to family tax benefits.
To quote Tony Abbott at the time, these are class war cuts that the government is inflicting on people.
This week, with barely a whimper, those cuts went through Parliament, unopposed by the coalition.
Well, what we see is that we will take a package of measures across the broad issues of taxation and family benefits.
But you oppose, you oppose, immediately after the budget.
And then you didn't back your words with action this week.
We are going to make responsible decisions about governing where we can.
In terms of, we will set out a clear set of policies, a clear set of initiatives.
But wasn't that a clear policy at the time?
The right now.
The class war cuts. He said that I am instinctively opposed to them, but they went through.
Well, at this point in time, we're going to set out in due course a very clear set of initiatives.
And I will make this guarantee that the cost of living for families will be lower under us.
The cost of living for pensioners and seniors will be lower under us.
And they will not face a massive hike in their electricity and petrol and gas and grocery prices.
Pennywell?
Well, you can't give that guarantee for two reasons.
One is you know that at the moment you have a very big black hole in the budget,
which would be in place where you're in government and that arises out of your black hole from the election.
I mean, I welcome the coalition actually deciding to pass some savings measures.
It's responsibility that was shown.
But I wonder whether it will continue.
I wonder whether Tony Abbott tomorrow will actually outline how he will fund these tax cuts that Greg's talking about.
But the second point about costs will be lower.
We've made clear that we will be putting in place proper assistance to Australian households for the carbon price.
And what is what Tony Abbott has made clear is he will claw that back.
Be very clear.
Tony Abbott, why?
I have to claw it back.
I'm getting the one up.
Yes, I'll.
Greg, I'm going to finish on a putt.
No, I'm going to finish on a question to both of you, which is completely partisan.
And I don't expect either of you to respond to the question. Pennywell, you first.
We're on Kevin Rudd tonight to a point because it's a year anniversary.

Tonight, the Prime Minister has announced that the tender process for the Australian network contract, which the ABC currently holds, has been delayed for six months and will now be a decision taken by Cabinet.
Previously, it was by default.
Why has it been taken out of Kevin Rudd's control?
I will look.
I don't have anything to add to the announcement.
Obviously, these are decisions of the government.
It is a big decision.
The Australian network is an important part of Australia's soft diplomacy.
But it was in Kevin Rudd's portfolio.
Well, it belongs to Cabinet.
Yeah. And the well, we're a government.
And Cabinet makes decisions about things in many portfolios, including my own, things that we think are in the national interest.
And this is no different from many decisions a government has and will make.
All right. And Greg Hunt on your side of politics, of course.
You've been having some headlines today just when you should be capitalising on the anniversary and the Labour Party about battles within your organisation,
or when, about the appointment of the new federal president, which will happen tomorrow, you've got the incumbent Alan Stockdale,
many saying that he should go in favour of Peter Reeth.
You've got Nick Mention saying that he's never seen such an act of treachery.
How concerned is this make the parliamentary wing of your party when the organisational wing is creating headlines like this on a day like this?
Well, the administrative wing of the party will make its decision.
It will be over by 9am tomorrow morning and by 9am one it will be ancient history.
I can tell you that the stories that come out of tomorrow will be the things that Tony Abbott has to say about the future for Australia,
the cost of living for Australian families, and the very simple vision that the DNA of lower taxes is who we are and the DNA of higher taxes and higher deficits is who they are.
So he'll be president Peter Reeth or Alan Stockdale.
I will leave that to the gods and to the electors.
Craig Hunter and Penny will.
Oh, come on, Craig.
Many things come on, Craig.
Thank you for joining us tonight on Late Line.
Good to speak with you.
